stem: Which statement about an undescended testis is most accurate?

options.text: A non-palpable testis is always ectopic
It may or may not be palpable
A non-palpable testis is always retractile

explanation: Undescended testis may or may not be palpable. Therefore, inability to feel the testis does not exclude cryptorchidism.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because an undescended testis is not always palpable.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because non-palpability does not mean the testis is always ectopic.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because an undescended testis may or may not be palpable.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because palpability is relevant outside puberty as part of the assessment of cryptorchidism.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a retractile testis is not defined as always non-palpable.
